title: On the Limitations of Cross-Lingual Consistency in Multilingual Text-to-image Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring text-to-image performance disparities (content generation quality and text rendering accuracy) across 10 different languages using multimodal evaluation metrics like CLIPScore, TRIGScore, and OCR to identify linguistic inequality.

Using a Vision-Language Model (VLM) as a judge to identify and extract culture-specific visual elements (e.g., clothing, architecture, objects) in images generated from semantically identical prompts translated into different languages.

Prompting a VLM-as-judge to classify the perceived race of subjects in generated images and calculating the normalized entropy of the resulting distribution to measure representational skew across different language prompts.

Prompting a VLM-as-judge to classify the perceived gender of subjects in generated images and calculating the normalized entropy of the resulting distribution to measure representational skew across different language prompts.

Prompting a VLM-as-judge to classify the perceived age group of subjects in generated images and calculating the normalized entropy of the resulting distribution to measure representational skew across different language prompts.
